subject: Discovery follow-up: Redwood demo & next steps
messages:
From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@aurora-analytics.com>, Priya Natarajan <priya@aurora-analytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 10 May 2027 11:20:00 -0700
Subject: Discovery follow-up: Redwood demo & next steps

Hi Samir / Priya —

Thanks again for taking the time today — really enjoyed learning more about Aurora's ingestion pipeline and the latency constraints on your customer-facing features. Quick recap and suggested next steps below: 

- What we covered: Redwood serving runtime, dedicated capacity options, and model-variant fallbacks for peak traffic.
- Your priorities: 1) 50k daily active users with 95th pct latency < 200ms; 2) strict data residency for EU customers (we flagged private deployment); 3) predictable per-token costs for budget planning.
- Open questions (from our side): what’s your current peak qps and the distribution of short vs long sequences? Also, who owns procurement vs security for contract review?

Suggested next steps:
1) I’ll share a short proposal / pricing tiers for Dedicated capacity (attached).
2) If you’re interested, we can schedule a 30-min session with Aditya to review architecture and performance expectations.
3) If procurement/security want docs, we can send our SOC2/arch compliance pack.

Can you confirm priority/timeline on this? If budget/timing has shifted, tell me and I’ll adjust the proposal.

Thanks — talk soon,
—Marissa
Marissa Cole | Account Executive
Redwood Inference
marissa.cole@redwood.ai | (415) 555-0192
Attachment: Redwood_Intro_Pricing.pdf (pdf, 340KB)
From: Samir Gupta <samir@aurora-analytics.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 17 May 2027 09:14:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Discovery follow-up: Redwood demo & next steps

Hi Marissa —

Appreciate the recap and the deck. We’ve been heads down with a sprint to finalize our rollout plan, so timing is tight. A couple quick notes:

- Could you send a simple SOW/estimate we can share with leadership? They’ll want monthly committed cost vs on-demand.
- Procurement may reach out separately (procure@aurora-analytics.com) for standard terms — I’ll loop them in when we have the numbers.

I’m not able to commit to a firm timeline yet, but we expect to prioritize this in our Q3 planning unless something shifts. Please go ahead and send the SOW/estimate and I’ll follow up.

Thanks,
Samir
Samir Gupta
Director of Product
Aurora Analytics

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.ai>
To: Samir Gupta <samir@aurora-analytics.com>
Cc: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 24 May 2027 10:02:00 -0700
Subject: Checking in — SOW/estimate + next steps

Hey Samir —

Just bumping this thread to see if you had a chance to review the estimate I sent last week (Redwood_Proposal_v1.pdf). Wanted to check whether the project is still likely to be prioritized into Q3. If your timeline shifted, no problem — I’m happy to adapt scope to fit a different budget or timeline.

If useful, Aditya is available to run a short technical deep-dive for your infra team — would 30 minutes next week help move things forward?

Quick options: Tue 6/1 10am PT, Wed 6/2 2pm PT — I can send calendar invites.

Thanks for the update either way —
Marissa

Hi Samir —

Wanted to close the loop on this one. I haven’t heard back after the proposal — totally understand you’re juggling priorities. If Aurora still plans to evaluate Redwood in Q3, I’m happy to leave the file open and schedule a technical session with Aditya. If you don’t plan to move forward, can I close the file on my side?

If closing, I’ll mark the opportunity as no-decision for now and reach back in a quarter. If you want one last thing (pricing tweak, procurement terms, or a short call), let me know and I’ll prioritize it.

Appreciate the transparency either way —
—Marissa
